title: Four Points, One Half
statement: Four points are chosen independently and uniformly on a circle. What is the probability that all four lie within some semicircle?
insight: Name the point the semicircle starts from: 'all others lie clockwise within π of point i' are disjoint events, each with probability (1/2)^3.
redHerring: Fixing one point and integrating over the arcs to the others in many cases.
hints: If the points fit in a semicircle, there is a natural 'first' point going clockwise.
Let $E_i$ be the event that the other three points lie within the half circle clockwise from point $i$. Can two $E_i$ happen at once?
solution:
If all points lie in a semicircle, exactly one point is the clockwise-first one; call this event $E_i$ for point $i$. The $E_i$ are disjoint (with probability 1).

$P(E_i) = (\tfrac12)^3$, since each other point independently falls in the half circle clockwise from point $i$. So the probability is $4\cdot\tfrac18 = \tfrac12$. In general it is $n/2^{n-1}$.
